verdict.root_cause: A traffic-shaping (netem) container was attached to cartservice's network namespace by platform-automation at 17:10:22, imposing a fixed 300ms delay with zero jitter on eth0 [tr_5564d0eaadf6]. Every cartservice cache round trip (HGET, HMSET) consequently costs ~300-305ms with no tail, cartservice's own handler adds only ~1-2ms on top, and end-to-end request time scales with the number of cart calls a request makes: ~605ms for a cart page view, ~1.5s for add-to-cart, ~2.47s for PlaceOrder where checkoutservice's span is almost entirely its two cart calls [tr_f6d9b79cbefc]. cartservice itself is healthy — serving continuously, no errors, no restarts, no connection failures in its logs [tr_98aaf0f638b5]. The failure mechanism is waiting on an artificially slowed cache path, and the alerts at frontend, checkoutservice and loadgenerator are downstream propagation of that wait. Unlike the prior identical injection cycles in the same window, which were removed after ~10 minutes, this one was still in place at onset [tr_5564d0eaadf6].
verdict.reasoning: The change record and the trace shape agree on a number. The netem attachment specifies delay=300ms jitter=0ms on cartservice's eth0 [tr_5564d0eaadf6]; the traces show a delay that is a fixed quantum, 300-305ms per cache operation, with no fast outliers and no long tail, which is what a constant injected delay looks like and is not what queuing, GC or contention looks like [tr_f6d9b79cbefc]. The delay is localised to the cart cache path: productcatalog, currency, payment, shipping, email and the order messaging hops in the same traces are all sub-20ms, ruling out a mesh-wide or generic network fault [tr_f6d9b79cbefc]. It is not inside cartservice application code, since the handler spans exceed the sum of their cache children by only ~1-2ms [tr_f6d9b79cbefc], and cartservice is not crashed, restarting, or losing its backing store — its logs show unbroken normal request handling with no error, connection or startup lines [tr_98aaf0f638b5]. Classification is dependency_latency rather than bad_config because the failure is the wait: the injected delay makes the cache round trip slow and the service fails by waiting for it. The netem container is a change record and evidence for the class, not the class. The two candidate configuration faults in the same change log — the v1.2.1 hotfix image and REDIS_ADDR pointing at port 6380 — were both reverted before onset (13 minutes and ~1.3h respectively) and so were not live [tr_5564d0eaadf6], which also excludes bad_deploy and a genuine bad_config. The metrics dispatches contribute nothing either way: the error-ratio series is empty in both incident and baseline windows, so it neither confirms nor excludes errors, and request rate, latency percentiles, restarts and readiness were never queried [tr_a61b629c1cb5][tr_52f590ff8f9f]. Remediation is removal of the traffic-shaping container — reverting that change record — which prior cycles show is the normal terminating action.
open_questions: The caller-side excess is unexplained. frontend client spans run ~604-613ms against ~302ms cartservice server spans, and checkoutservice client spans run ~1206-1216ms against ~301-303ms server spans [tr_f6d9b79cbefc]. That excess is itself a multiple of 300ms, which suggests gRPC retries or per-attempt connection cost, but only one server span is recorded per call and nothing in the dispatches confirms retry behaviour or client-side timeout settings at frontend or checkoutservice.

Whether the injection has since been removed is unknown. The prior cycles lasted ~10 minutes and this one was ~3 minutes old at onset [tr_5564d0eaadf6]; no dispatch checked the current state of the cartservice network namespace, so the incident may already be self-resolving.

cartservice's actual error behaviour was never measured. The error-ratio series is absent in both windows and four of five requested metric signals were never queried [tr_a61b629c1cb5][tr_52f590ff8f9f], so whether the latency escalated into timeouts or dropped requests at any caller is unestablished.
The log query returned only the oldest 8 and newest 32 lines; the interval containing 17:13:30 itself was not retrieved [tr_98aaf0f638b5], so no cartservice log evidence covers the onset minute.

No dispatch examined redis-cart directly, so an independent contemporaneous cache-side degradation stacked on top of the injected 300ms cannot be excluded, only rendered unnecessary as an explanation.
Triage reports 4 unmeasured edges crossed; which service pairs those are, and whether any carries additional latency, was not resolved by any dispatch.

Why this injection cycle produced an incident when at least seven earlier identical cycles in the same 24h window apparently did not [tr_5564d0eaadf6] — duration, concurrent load, or alert threshold — is unsettled.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself became slow, adding ~300ms to every cart cache operation independent of the netem attachment.
alternatives.why_not: A change record specifying exactly delay=300ms jitter=0ms on cartservice's eth0 landed 3 minutes before onset [tr_5564d0eaadf6], and the observed delay is a fixed quantum with zero spread and no tail [tr_f6d9b79cbefc] — a loaded or degraded Redis produces a distribution, not a constant. The coincidence of the injected value and the measured value leaves this needing an unexplained second cause. It is not fully excluded, since no dispatch inspected redis-cart directly.

alternatives.root_cause: gRPC client retry or connection settings at frontend and checkoutservice multiply a modest cart slowdown into 2x and 4x caller-side latency, making the callers the primary amplifier of impact.
alternatives.why_not: This can at best explain the unaccounted caller-side multiples, not the underlying ~300ms, which is present at the cache operation itself inside cartservice [tr_f6d9b79cbefc]. Removing the injected delay would collapse the caller totals regardless of retry policy, and no change record touching checkoutservice or frontend configuration appears near onset [tr_5564d0eaadf6]. It remains a live contributor to severity rather than a root cause.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed. The fault is a netem container attached to cartservice's network namespace imposing 300ms/0ms-jitter on eth0 [tr_5564d0eaadf6], seen as cache round trips at 300-305ms with no tail [tr_f6d9b79cbefc]. The fix is detaching that container, which none of the three available actions performs. revert_config cannot apply: the config changes in history (REDIS_ADDR, image tag) were both already reverted before onset and are ruled out; there is no config value to restore. If the injection is removed out-of-band, Jaeger should show HGET/HMSET drop to single-digit ms and PlaceOrder fall from ~2.47s to well under 100ms.
proposal.if_wrong: Re-sample cartservice traces 15 minutes on. If cache spans are still ~300ms, the injection persists and needs an out-of-band detach plus escalation to platform-automation. If they are already normal, it self-resolved as prior cycles did.
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves ~605ms cart pages and ~2.47s PlaceOrder in place; if any caller timeout sits below those, latency becomes dropped orders, and error behaviour is currently unmeasurable. Acting instead would be worse: revert_config or restart_service on cartservice recreates the container without removing the netem attachment, causing an outage that fixes nothing.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change. frontend, checkoutservice and loadgenerator continue to see the propagated latency until the injection is removed.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services alerted in a tight window starting at cartservice and spreading to checkoutservice and frontend, which is a propagating failure rather than an isolated warning. No open incidents to fold this into, so it warrants investigation with cartservice as the likely origin.
